source.title: On The Presence of Double-Descent in Deep Reinforcement Learning
source.authors: V. Veselý; Aleksandar Todorov; M. Sabatelli

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper argues that double descent occurs in deep reinforcement learning, but its reported measurement is policy entropy, not test error or generalization. It neither tests the listed claim versions with the measure they name nor uses the finding as a tool.
record.gate_note: The paper reports policy-entropy trends across training episodes and interprets them as evidence of double descent. It does not report test error, an interpolation threshold, or measured generalization outcomes. Record the entropy findings under fits_no_version, not as results for the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The paper asserts epoch-wise double descent (V2) and a possible triple descent (V6) in A2C on Frozen-Lake. Its only measure, however, is policy entropy, a confidence or uncertainty score rather than test error, return or generalization. No interpolation threshold is located, and no out-of-distribution performance is measured; the authors defer that to future work. Because the construct differs from what any version names, the entropy findings go under fits_no_version and no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right but understates the authors' claims. They say the results show a clear epoch-wise DD curve and establish DD as a factor in DRL. They attribute the second descent to implicit regularization toward flat minima. They also concede that whether entropy compression reflects better OOD generalization still has to be evaluated. These claims rest on entropy alone.
record.recipe_differences: Unlike the original supervised-learning test-error analyses, this study uses A2C on Frozen-Lake and tracks policy entropy over episodes; it does not measure test error or locate an interpolation threshold.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported entropy dynamics differ by architecture: the smaller configurations reportedly reach near-zero entropy rapidly, while [128, 128, 128] retains higher entropy and [64, 64, 64] shows a re-ascent.

fits_no_version.finding: The [64] and [64,64] A2C backbones converge to near-zero policy entropy within about 2,000 episodes on Frozen-Lake.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Smaller A2C backbones collapse policy entropy quickly on Frozen-Lake.

fits_no_version.finding: The [64,64,64] backbone shows an entropy descent, then a re-ascent around episode 3,500, then a final descent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Policy entropy can follow a non-monotone, multi-phase trajectory during A2C training.

fits_no_version.finding: The [128,128,128] backbone keeps higher mean entropy and larger variance for an extended period.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The largest A2C backbone retains higher and more variable policy entropy for longer.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 7th Northern Lights Deep Learning Conference (NLDL), PMLR V, 2026
record.problems: The paper does not report test-error or out-of-distribution generalization measurements, despite interpreting entropy as evidence of double descent. It describes the findings as preliminary and says formal evaluation of generalization remains future work. The reported outcomes are qualitative; numerical curve values are not given in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version results were omitted; the paper reports no test-error or generalization outcomes for those versions.

untested.parts: Five capacities are compared, but only on entropy. There is no test-error or return measure against model size and no interpolation point.
The paper claims an epoch-wise DD curve, but only policy entropy is tracked over episodes. No test-error or generalization curve is reported.
There is no risk-versus-capacity curve and no other model classes.
A multi-phase entropy pattern for [64,64,64] is likened to triple descent, but no test-error peaks are measured. Label noise and regularization are not varied.

record.verdict_notes: This is a two-page workshop abstract. The text says models 'pass the interpolation point' and that generalization 'degrades then improves'. Neither quantity is measured: Figure 1 plots only entropy, and no numeric values are given. Rows R1–R5 are correctly unlinked and marked cannot_determine. This is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No test-error sweep over model size or measured interpolation point.
No test-error measurement over training epochs; policy entropy is measured instead.
No training-sample-size sweep near an interpolation threshold.
No risk-versus-capacity tests across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested across size, epochs, or sample count.
No label-noise or regularization conditions are tested, and no peak count in test error is measured.
No effective-parameter-count analysis or test-error curve is reported.
